source_pr_title: fix(ci): release-tag falls back to second-parent subject on merge commits (bro-zra)
author: kilo-code-bot
body:
**SUGGESTION:** Fallback only inspects the second parent's *tip* subject

If any commit lands on the release branch after `release: v$v` (e.g. a manual fix pushed before merge), the tip subject no longer matches and the merge silently skips tagging — the same silent-skip class this PR fixes. `release.yml` force-pushes a clean single-commit branch so this only bites manual follow-ups, but searching the second parent's own commits instead of just its tip closes it:

```suggestion
            subject=$(git log --format=%s "HEAD^2" --not "HEAD^1" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 "^release: v" || true)
```

The exact-version gate at line 54 still validates whatever this extracts, so stale `release: v*` subjects from main's ancestry (excluded by `--not HEAD^1`) can't false-positive.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.
